description:
FILED s537a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-10) as #4703's residue.  PRE-EXISTING (main 4a39a1c7 the same).  A loud DROP, not silent.

    no warnings;
    sub isa { "isa(" . join(" ", @_) . ")" }
    my @d = (isa 7, 8); print scalar(@d), " @d\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  1 isa(7 8)
      PCL:          PCL: statement dropped at ... line 3: my @d = (isa 7, 8); -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []

`isa(1, 2)` with parens is right since #4603 (runtime-name-hygiene-01.t).  The paren-less word is classified by Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::is_token_operator from Config's precedence table (`'isa' => { assoc => 'x', no => 2, prec => 50 }`), so handle_subcalls skips it as "a word-form binary operator" (PExpr.pm `next if $self->is_token_operator($now)`) whatever the feature state.  perl's `isa` is an infix operator ONLY where the `isa` feature is in force (5.32+, in the :5.36 bundle); elsewhere it is an ordinary identifier.

Fix direction: the word-operator classification of `isa` asks the same one answer as the other gated keywords -- Pl::Parser::gated_keyword_at (s537a's PExpr::_gated_sub_here reads it from a head token) -- at the classification site, so `$o isa Foo` under the feature stays infix and a user sub call without it is a call.  Measure first: is_token_operator has many callers (every token test in PExpr); the gate must be asked only for the Word `isa`.  s537a did not take it: it changes the token classifier, a different site from the operand grammar #4703 fixed.  Probe: scratch/s537a/p/m4a.pl's removed line in the s537a worktree.


=== DONE (s537a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-10 .. 11-13; commit bada882f, with #4703 on the s537a branch, rebased over MAIN-READY-87; shas as of the rebase over main b620405f) ===
FIXED by #4703's resume: `PExpr::is_token_operator` answers the word `isa` as the infix operator only where the keyword is (`_gated_sub_here`), so `sub isa { ... } my @d = (isa 7, 8)` calls the sub (perl `isa(7 8)`), and `main->isa('main')` still dispatches.  Guard Pl/t/runtime-name-hygiene-01.t row 21 (its line 11).  Probes m4h (fixed), m4i (infix isa under the feature, control), m4j (a class overriding UNIVERSAL::isa, control).
